page: Microsoft Azure E16-8ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine within the EDSv5 series, provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware-level support includes AVX-512 extensions, AES cryptography, and SHA-NI acceleration. The instance is equipped with 128 GB of RAM, yielding an elevated ratio of 16 GB of memory per vCPU. Ephemeral local storage is provided via an integrated 644 GB solid-state drive, while no hardware accelerators or GPUs are included.

Benchmark measurements place the instance within median performance bands across compute and memory operations. The server produces a Geekbench single-core score of 1,633.0 and a multi-core score of 6,133.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 11,443.28. In memory bandwidth evaluations, the platform achieves 419.39 GB/sec for small-block cached reads and 58.16 GB/sec for large-block transfers. High throughput is sustained in key-value operations, with Redis handling 7.87 million SET operations per second. Tradeoffs appear in multi-threaded decompression and localized 7B model LLM inference, where performance falls into lower percentiles due to the limited four-core physical layout.

The constrained compute core count paired with a large memory footprint creates qualitative resource efficiency for licensing and hosting environments where memory capacity is the primary constraint. Rather than paying for surplus vCPUs to gain memory scale, this configuration targets memory-heavy demands without compute overprovisioning. The E16-8ds_v5 is appropriate for in-memory caching layers such as Redis, relational and NoSQL database management systems, data processing pipelines, and general enterprise workloads with substantial working memory requirements.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-8ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the instance provides 128 GB of RAM, delivering a high memory allocation of 16 GB per vCPU. Local scratch capacity is supplied via an integrated 644 GB SSD, with zero GPUs present. Standard CPU and memory evaluations place the system firmly within average performance brackets, generating 7.87 million Redis SET operations per second and maintaining a PassMark database operations metric of 4,064.08. Due to its constrained physical core count, multi-threaded throughput and local 7B LLM inference show weaker results relative to larger instances. This configuration is efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand extensive parallel compute, including in-memory caches, enterprise databases, and ETL processing.
